newsitem.title: USA: Dell tops list of top stock performers - study.
newsitem.headline: Dell tops list of top stock performers - study.

text.p: Michael Dell of Dell Computer Corp. topped the list of chief executives who delivered the highest total return to their shareholders in 1996, a top executive search firm said Wednesday.
Heidrick & Struggles, in its first annual list of "High Impact CEOs," said Dell had a total return of 198 percent to shareholders.
Bernard Cammarata, president and CEO of TJX Cos Inc., ranked second after TJX returned a total of 154 percent to shareholders.

The top 10 performers were calculated based on total return to shareholders -- share appreciation plus dividends -- as a percentage for the full year 1996, Heidrick said. The analysis was limited to companies in the Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks.

"While there are obviously many ways to evaluate a CEO's performance, we believe a company's total return to shareholders is the simplest and purest indicator of value creation," said John Thompson, vice chairman of Heidrick.
C.R. Palmer of Rowan Cos Inc. ranked third, based on Rowan's total return of 132 percent for the year, while Intel Corp.'s Andrew Grove was fourth at 123.9 percent.
Floyd English of Andrew Corp. was fifth, followed by EMC Corp.'s Michael Ruettgers and Michael Birck of Tellabs Inc., Heidrick said.
Rounding out the top 10 were Microsoft Corp.'s Bill Gates, Robert Keiser of Oryx Energy Co. and Leon Hirsch of U.S. Surgical Corp.
